caption: Authentication
description: Authentication events report authentication session activities, including user attempts to log on or log off, regardless of success, as well as other key stages within the authentication process. These events are typically generated by authentication services, such as Kerberos, OIDC, or SAML, and may include information about the user, the authentication method used, and the status of the authentication attempt.
name: authentication

1.caption: Logon
1.description: A new logon session was requested.

2.caption: Logoff
2.description: A logon session was terminated and no longer exists.

3.caption: Authentication Ticket
3.description: A Kerberos authentication ticket (TGT) was requested.

4.caption: Service Ticket Request
4.description: A Kerberos service ticket was requested.

5.caption: Service Ticket Renew
5.description: A Kerberos service ticket was renewed.

7.caption: Account Switch
7.description: A utility or service switched the user account. See the account_switch_type_id attribute for more details.

auth_factors.description: Describes a category of methods used for identity verification in an authentication attempt.

authentication_token.description: The authentication token, ticket, or assertion, e.g. Kerberos, OIDC, SAML.

references.description: RFC 4120: The Kerberos Network Authentication Service (V5)
The OASIS Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) V2.0

certificate.description: The certificate associated with the authentication or pre-authentication (Kerberos).

dst_endpoint.description: The endpoint to which the authentication was targeted.

grant_type.description: The OAuth 2.0 authorization grant type, normalized to the caption of the grant_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

grant_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the OAuth 2.0 authorization grant that the client used to obtain its tokens, for example when auth_protocol_id is OAUTH 2.0 or OpenID. Use 0 (Unknown) when the grant cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with the source specific value in grant_type when the grant is not listed.

1.caption: Authorization Code
1.description: The client redirects the user to the authorization server to sign in, and exchanges the authorization code it receives for tokens.

2.caption: Implicit
2.description: The authorization server returns the access token directly in the redirect, without an authorization code.

3.caption: Resource Owner Password Credentials
3.description: The client collects the user name and password itself and sends them to the authorization server for tokens.

references.description: RFC 6749 section 4.3 Resource Owner Password Credentials Grant

4.caption: Client Credentials
4.description: The client authenticates as itself, without a user, with its own credentials such as a client secret or certificate.

5.caption: Refresh Token
5.description: The client exchanges a refresh token for a new access token.

references.description: RFC 6749 section 6 Refreshing an Access Token

6.caption: Device Code
6.description: The device shows a code that the user enters on another device to sign in, while the device polls the authorization server for tokens. Used by devices with limited input.

7.caption: JWT Bearer
7.description: The client presents a signed JSON Web Token as the authorization grant.

references.description: RFC 7523 JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Client Authentication and Authorization Grants

8.caption: SAML 2.0 Bearer
8.description: The client presents a SAML 2.0 assertion as the authorization grant.

references.description: RFC 7522 Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0 Profile for OAuth 2.0 Client Authentication and Authorization Grants

9.caption: Token Exchange
9.description: The client exchanges a security token it already holds for a different token, for example to act on behalf of a user.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The grant type is not mapped. See the grant_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

is_remote.description: The attempted authentication is over a remote connection.

service.description: The service or gateway to which the user or process is being authenticated

status_detail.description:
The details about the authentication request. For example, possible details for Windows logon or logoff events are:
  • Success
    • LOGOFF_USER_INITIATED
    • LOGOFF_OTHER
  • Failure
    • USER_DOES_NOT_EXIST
    • INVALID_CREDENTIALS
    • ACCOUNT_DISABLED
    • ACCOUNT_LOCKED_OUT
    • PASSWORD_EXPIRED

user.description: The subject (user/role or account) to authenticate.
